title: Marrow and peach on toast with goat's cheese

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Marrow, peaches, garlic, bread, goat's cheese, olive oil, lemon and mint are all whole foods a grandparent might have kept, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Tesco sells sourdough, soft goat's cheese, peaches and marrow at everyday prices in late August.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan and a toaster or grill, and the techniques are peeling, cubing, frying and toasting.

works.reason: One small marrow fried until golden, plus garlic, chilli and lemon, piled on four thick slices of toast with goat's cheese and peach makes a sensible, well-seasoned light lunch for four.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is fair for peeling, seeding and cubing a small marrow, slicing garlic and peaches and toasting bread, and the 10-minute cook matches the 8 to 10 minutes of frying plus 1 minute for the garlic.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item is used, including the lemon, mint, chilli flakes and both portions of the oil, nothing unlisted appears, and sourdough is a fair name for crusty bread.

seasonal_feel.reason: Marrow is the bulk of the topping and the point of the dish, and peaches with mint suit a warm last day of August.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English instructions a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a proper lunch of vegetables, fruit, cheese and bread that a family would happily eat again.
